answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square in the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), with a negatively weighted one-pixel border around it (row 0, column 0, row 4, column 4).
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/artifact patch in corner
answer.mechanism: Several first-layer units detect a bright 3x3 corner patch. Units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29 carry large positive weights on the patch and negative weights on its border, which makes them a 'bright square on dark background' detector. These units feed layer-2 units u3 and u10 strongly (e.g. u10 takes +89 from unit 0, +99 from unit 1, +77 from unit 8, +74 from unit 18, +73 from unit 29). u3 and u10 have positive output weights (+65, +64). The same units suppress u0, u6, u8 and u15 (weights of about -50 to -95), and those layer-2 units have large negative output weights (-90, -99, -82, -89). A second group, units 9, 21, 24 and 27, has high biases (73-99) and strongly negative patch weights (-58 to -81). These units feed u0, u6, u8 and u15, so the patch switches off a benign-voting pathway. Both routes push the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: The weights on rows 1-3, cols 1-3 are about +55 to +99 in units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29, and about -58 to -81 in units 9, 21, 24 and 27. No other region of the weight grids has magnitudes this large. In the same units, row 0, col 0 and row 4 (cols 0-3) carry the opposite sign (about -20 to -40, or +20 to +40), forming a crisp square template far from the nodule. Real anatomy would not produce an identical sharp 3x3 template in 11 of 32 units. The remaining units (3-7, 10-17, 19, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28, 30, 31) look like untrained noise with weights of ±10.
answer.main_feature: Genuine nodule features: units 9, 21, 24 and 27 respond to a small, compact bright core at the centre (rows 10-13, cols 10-13) and vote benign. Units 0, 1, 8, 18 and 29 respond to brightness in a ring or region around and below the centre (rows 13-16), with negative weight on the central core, and vote malignant; together with the broadly positive units 2 and 20, this means larger, more extensive or irregular dense tissue reads as malignant.
